_comment: Two tiles at the compress projections -- the production cut, re-measured here and confirmed optimal. Whole network composes on CPU only (59.775 ms int8, 98.564 fp32; DSP rejects it with 'Param[0] has incorrect Value 1', HTA with 'unsupported op StridedSlice'). Cutting at /compress_obs_enc/Gemm_output_0 puts the encoders on the DSP (16.339 ms) and leaves the transformer on CPU fp32 (13.741 ms): 30.080 ms of critical path, half of it off the CPU. A third cut between the two encoders (vint_k3_enc) does not help -- 30.633 ms -- because a contiguous slice cannot express the two encoders as parallel tiles; their topological order in the ONNX serialises them. Note the gap in the op ranges (ops 0-5 and 1070 are absent): those are constant subgraphs -- nodes whose value does not depend on any graph input -- and they belong to every tile that needs them rather than to one. Assigning such a node to a single tile makes its output cross the cut as a tensor, which the converter rejects (KeyError on the promoted Constant) and the quantizer cannot calibrate. ViNT has 610 of them.
